definitions.explanation: Facts, information, and skills acquired through experience or education.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}の{知識|ちしき}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
{知識|ちしき}を{広|ひろ}げたい。
examples.english: I want to expand my knowledge.

examples.japanese: その{知識|ちしき}は{仕事|しごと}に{役立|やくだ}つ。
examples.english: That knowledge is useful for work.

examples.japanese: {専門|せんもん}{知識|ちしき}がないと、この{仕事|しごと}は{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: Without specialized knowledge, this work is difficult.

examples.japanese: {大学|だいがく}で{学|まな}んだ{知識|ちしき}を{社会|しゃかい}に{出|で}てから{活|い}かしたいと{思|おも}っている。
examples.english: I want to make use of the knowledge I learned at university after entering society.

notes:
{知識|ちしき} refers to information and understanding acquired through learning or experience.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {知識|ちしき}がある: to have knowledge
- {知識|ちしき}を{得|え}る: to gain knowledge
- {知識|ちしき}を{広|ひろ}げる: to expand one's knowledge
- {知識|ちしき}を{身|み}につける: to acquire knowledge

COMPOUNDS:
- {専門|せんもん}{知識|ちしき}: specialized knowledge
- {基礎|きそ}{知識|ちしき}: basic knowledge
- {予備|よび}{知識|ちしき}: prior knowledge
- {知識人|ちしきじん}: intellectual, learned person

CONTRAST:
- {知識|ちしき}: factual knowledge
- {知恵|ちえ}: wisdom (practical application of knowledge)
